name: Sanctions & coercion
summary: EU's proposed 22nd Russia package would cut about 60 banks from SWIFT and list 70+ ships; still awaiting member states
state: The European Commission proposed the EU's 22nd Russia sanctions package on 23 Nov: about 60 Russian banks removed from SWIFT, a ban on helping repair Russian refineries, more than 70 shadow-fleet vessels and a ban on Russian-insured tankers (Xinhua). It remains a proposal needing member-state approval (Sofia Globe). On 16 Nov the EU had already listed 113 Russian targets, including 49 banks and financial firms (Ukrainska Pravda). No major economy is fully cut off from payment systems, so Watch holds.
for_you: Firms with links to Russian banks, shipping, energy services or crypto platforms face wider compliance checks if the package is adopted. Official guidance for UK businesses is published by OFSI and the Department for Business and Trade.
rubric_hit: Major new package proposed (EU 22nd: ~60 banks off SWIFT, 70+ vessels) = Watch; no major economy fully cut off

sources.title: Xinhua — European Commission proposes 22nd round of sanctions against Russia

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
